text:
alertbot: INCIDENT: elevated error rate observed for /v1/generate across eu-west-1. Paging on-call. Alerts: log-based 'generate-5xx-spike' firing.

sara (oncall): I'm on it — pulling logs and traces now. any immediate customer hits?

matt: I'm seeing a spike in returning 502/503 with message 'upstream connection reset'. A lot of entries like:
```
level=error svc=runtime msg=\"upstream request failed\" err=\"connection reset by peer\" model=redwood-moderate request_id=...
```

emily: Confirmed. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/latency/generate-overview?orgId=1 shows tail latency up ~3x in last 5m. SLO errors increasing.

jordan: No customer-facing 5xx spike in the tracker yet, but several large customers reported slow responses in support threads. tagging @support.

kevin: Temporarily throttling non-essential background batches in eu-west-1 to free capacity. Will monitor.

ops-bot: automation: muted alert generate-5xx-spike for 15m while mitigation ongoing. Reason: live mitigation by oncall.

sara (oncall): Thanks. Two parallel actions: 1) live mitigation to reduce customer impact, 2) short-term alert tuning to prevent noisy pages for known transient errors.

matt: For tuning, propose we update the log-based alert query to exclude the known transient signature and only fire on sustained counts. Current Loki-ish query: `count_over_time({svc=\"runtime\", path=\"/v1/generate\"} |~ \"connection reset by peer\" [5m]) > 20`

matt: Proposed change: add regex filter for backend-originated resets vs client aborts. e.g.: `|~ \"(connection reset by peer|EOF while reading from backend)\"` -> too broad. So we add a signature to detect *backend-side* socket resets that correlate with other fields: `| regexp \"backend=([a-z0-9_-]+)\" and status=5..`

emily: I can craft a safer exclusion. Suggest we instead add a negative lookahead for `client_abort` tag and increase window to 10m and threshold to 50 for a region-level alert. New alert draft:
```
expr: count_over_time({svc=\"runtime\", path=\"/v1/generate\"} |= \"status=5\" |~ "(?i)connection reset by peer"[10m]) > 50
```
and in the query layer, exclude `client_abort=true` events: `|~ \"client_abort=false\"`
```

jordan: Agree on increasing window. Also propose adding a cheap signature to detect the known transient failure cause we saw earlier: `KVCacheEvictError` followed by connection reset within 2s. Pattern: `message: \'KVCacheEvictError.*\\n.*connection reset by peer\'`. That we can surface to ops only, not page.

sara (oncall): Good. Action list:
- matt: prepare rule change (exclude client abort events + bump window) and push as a canary to eu-west-1 non-prod logs by 1942006120.
- emily: add dashboard panel highlighting new signature counts and link to incident doc.
- jordan: open a ticket SUP-4219 for customer impact tracking and note any customers who reported slowness.
- kevin: continue capacity mitigation, revert after 20m if stable.

matt: pushing draft alert rule now. snippet to be deployed (Loki alert manager format):
```
- alert: generate-5xx-spike
  expr: |
    sum by(region) (count_over_time({svc=\"runtime\", path=\"/v1/generate\"} |= \"status=5\" |~ \"(?i)connection reset by peer\" |~ \"client_abort=false\"[10m])) > 50
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/12345/generate-5xx-spike
```

matt: I'll canary it on non-prod logs first.

ops-bot: automation: submitted canary deployment job #canary-873 to logging-rule-service.

emily: I've added a temporary dashboard panel showing `KVCacheEvictError -> connection reset` co-occurrence counts. link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/kvchain-failures.

jordan: SUP-4219 created and linked. Noted 3 customers (orgs: AcmeCorp, FinApp, EduLabs) reported slow responses between 19:02-19:18 UTC. No confirmed data loss.

sara (oncall): Good. We'll hold pages to eng-sre unless the rule shows persistent high counts after canary. Keep ops-bot muting in 15m windows as needed.

kevin: Capacity mitigation showing reduced latency after throttling background batches. tail p95 back to near baseline in eu-west-1.

matt: Canary rule deployed to non-prod. If stable for 10m I'll promote to prod logging ruleset.

emily: Quick note for post-incident: we should add a long-term signature rather than excluding via regex. Exclusion risks hiding real regressions. Proposal: create a non-paging 'known-transient' tag and a separate alert that aggregates those counts for weekly trend analysis.

sara (oncall): Agreed. Add to postmortem actions. For now: if canary looks good, promote and unmute alerts. If not, we'll rollback and do more granular signature work.

ops-bot: automation: canary job #canary-873 succeeded.

matt: Promoting to prod ruleset now.

ops-bot: automation: updated alert generate-5xx-spike in prod with new query. muted state cleared.

jordan: Noted. I've informed support and customers about temporary throttle and status.

sara (oncall): Wrapping up. Summary in incident channel later plus postmortem with RCA and follow-up (add signature, long-term dashboard, runbook update). Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
